reference_frame.type: local East-North-Up tangent plane (WGS84 -> ECEF -> ENU)
reference_frame.origin_is: OSM node/2451905265, aeroway=threshold ref=17L - the paved threshold of runway 17L, i.e. where an aircraft departing south on the eastern runway lines up. Start of the takeoff roll.
reference_frame.why_this_origin: 17L is the eastern runway (facing 17 = facing south, so 'left' = east). Departing 17L southbound puts the LATAM maintenance base, the LATAM ramp and the SCL control tower on the aircraft's RIGHT, ~1.5 to 3 km into the roll - the frame a LATAM employee at SCL would recognise.
reference_frame.z_convention: All z are 0 in this file: this is a PLAN, not a terrain. Ground height belongs to the terrain task.
reference_frame.curvature_note: Exact ENU was used, so points far from the origin have a true 'up' below the tangent plane. Worst value in this dataset is -5.33 m (earth curvature over ~8.2 km). It is dropped from the output; if the scene is built flat, that is the error you are accepting.
reference_frame.inverse: lat/lon can be recovered by inverting the ENU rotation about (origin_lat, origin_lon) on the WGS84 ellipsoid.

cross_check.method: OSM is one source. Runway geometry was re-checked against two independent sources. Anything only one source knows is flagged.

17L/35R.verdict: CONFIRMED ~3750 m - three independent sources within 4 m.

17R/35L.verdict: CONFIRMED 3800 m by OSM (tag AND geometry) and Wikipedia. OurAirports' length field says 12303 ft for BOTH runways, which is a copy error: its own 17R endpoint coordinates imply ~3883 m. OurAirports' length is discarded here.

true_bearing.verdict: CONFIRMED ~177.4 deg true. OurAirports rounds to whole degrees and brackets the computed value.

displaced_threshold_35R.verdict: CONFIRMED ~545 m. Two independent sources agree within 7 m. This is real: 35R landings touch down ~545 m north of the southern pavement end. 17L departures use the full length.

centerline_separation.verdict: CONFIRMED ~1555 m (+/- 10 m between sources). Wide-spaced parallels - well above the ~1310 m needed for independent parallel approaches, which is why SCL runs both runways at once.

runway_width.osm: NOT MAPPED. No width tag on either runway and no area:aeroway pavement polygon exists for SCL - the runways are centerlines only.
runway_width.wikipedia: Says the ORIGINAL runway (today 17L/35R) was 3200 m x 45 m when built; gives no current width.
runway_width.verdict: NOT ESTABLISHED - do not treat width as known. 45 m (148 ft) is the standard ICAO code E/F width and is what OurAirports gives for 17R/35L, so 45 m is the reasonable working value. The 180 ft (54.9 m) OurAirports gives for 17L/35R is NOT a standard width and is single-source; it may be pavement-plus-shoulders or simply wrong. If the width matters visually, get it from the Chilean AIP (DGAC) AD 2 SCEL. It is deliberately left null in this file.

field_elevation.osm: not tagged on the aerodrome relation
field_elevation.verdict: The two sources disagree by ~6 m. Not resolved here - this belongs to the terrain task, which should settle it.

cross_check.history_note: Wikipedia: the second runway (17R/35L) opened 1 Sep 2005; the older runway was then redesignated 17L/35R. So the eastern runway is the original one, and the LATAM base and the terminals grew up around it.

departure_17L_landmarks.explanation: Every named feature projected onto the 17L takeoff roll. 'distance_along_roll_m' is metres from the 17L threshold (the origin) measured along the runway; 'side' is which side of the aircraft it passes on while rolling south on 17L.
departure_17L_landmarks.note: An A320 rotates somewhere around 1500-1900 m into the roll, so the LATAM base at 1287 m is abeam just BEFORE rotation and stays in frame, off the right side, through liftoff.
